- Environment: node 18, redwood-inference v1.3.1
- API key: dev key (not the prod key)

- Error: HTTP 502/504 intermittently; response body is empty or contains "Upstream error".

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 26 Jun 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Great demo — next steps for SDK/auth + integration debugging

Alex — thanks for the repro. Quick troubleshooting checklist while I loop in engineering: 

1) Can you share the exact curl (or set curl_repro.sh) that reproduces the 502? That helps our gateway traces match the request.
2) For embeddings, we recommend batches <= 8 for the dev endpoint; for production you can use dedicated capacity which supports larger batches.
3) Timeouts: the server-side processing for large batches can exceed 30s; setting your client timeout to 120s is a safe short-term mitigation.
4) Please add the header X-Redwood-Trace: <random-id> so we can locate the trace in our logs.

Cc'ing Neha (ops) to look at routing and whether your requests hit our hosted pool or were routed to a fallback model variant — that can cause intermittent 5xxs if capacity spikes.

If you can send the curl and the X-Trace id I’ll escalate to engineering with a concrete repro.

— Marissa

From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Alex Johnson <alex.j@finlytics.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 27 Jun 2026 08:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Great demo — initial triage notes (routing + payload)

Alex — Priyom from Platform/Infra here. Thanks for the logs. I pulled the support trace you attached (support_trace.log) and a couple quick findings: 

- The requests from your dev key are hitting the hosted pool but intermittently routed to a fallback instance where the model variant had a higher memory footprint; during GC spikes the instance returned a 502.
- The payload you attached is ~1.2MB (encoded) with 12 items. Our gateway has a transient failure threshold for >1MB payloads on the hosted dev pool.
- Repro steps that will help us triage immediately:
  * Run the attached curl_repro.sh which posts the same payload and sets X-Redwood-Trace.
  * If you can reproduce, send the trace id back and we'll pull full worker logs.

Short-term mitigations:
- Reduce batch size to 6 or fewer OR compress payloads (we support gzip)
- Increase client timeout to 120s
- If you want a durable fix, we can provision a short-lived dedicated capacity for your account to validate large-batch throughput (requires brief approvals) — Marissa can scope.

I’ve attached the support_trace.log and a curl repro helper. 

— Priyom
Platform Infra | Redwood Inference
priyom@redwood.com

From: Alex Johnson <alex.j@finlytics.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 28 Jun 2026 07:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Great demo — initial triage notes (routing + payload)

Thanks Priyom — that helps a lot. We ran curl_repro.sh and reproduced consistently with trace id rwd-trace-20260628-7a9f. Log excerpt (attached) shows the 502 from the gateway and a short-lived "upstream timeout" in the worker logs. Couple of follow-ups from our side:

- We're evaluating reducing batch size to 6 for now. What's the expected token throughput tradeoff?
- For reranker: are there separate routing rules vs embeddings? We send embeddings then a rerank pass to the same model family — are those considered different endpoints?
- For structured output/tool calling: can you share the sample schema for the reranker output we discussed (we want score + action suggestion).

Also, can we get a short 30-minute troubleshooting slot today or tomorrow to run the traces live? We have engineers on standby.

— Alex

Attachments: support_trace.log (repro), sample_request.json (updated)
